verdict.rationale: Notion documents several scoped credential types. Internal connections are limited to a single workspace with a static token, PATs act as one user, public OAuth connections have a chosen installation scope, and an agent-API connection can access only Custom Agents explicitly shared with it. Least-privilege control is shown only at the workspace, user and explicit-sharing level, not as fine-grained permission scopes. Missing for 10: documented fine-grained capability scopes (e.g., read-only vs write, per-resource content restrictions), token expiry/rotation controls, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Internal connections are scoped to a single workspace and use a static API token.
Personal access tokens (PATs) are user-scoped tokens for scripts, CLI workflows, Workers, and tools that should act as one Notion user.
At creation time, you choose their installation scope
The connection can access only Custom Agents that are explicitly shared with it.
